alignments.note: Waw takes And (rule 14).
The conditional particle im takes if.
Cognate infinitive absolute takes the intensifier at all, one rendering written in two words (rule 56); headed on the content word all (rule 24).
Finite verb keeps the auxiliary do and the lexical hide, discontinuous around the intensifier (rule 25).
Construct noun takes the supplied the; the rectum's own article takes the written the standing before its own word (rule 29, arthrous case).
Article on the rectum takes the the standing before its own word.
Nomen rectum takes of the land, headed on land (rule 19).
Object marker H853 with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Noun takes eyes.
Suffix takes the possessive their (rule 18).
Preposition takes from (rule 11).
Article on ish; the single determiner the ASV writes is the demonstrative that, which the written pronoun hu takes (rules 18, 41).
Noun takes man.
Article on the demonstrative; no separate the is written.
Demonstrative pronoun takes the determiner that written for it (rule 18).
Temporal preposition before the infinitive construct takes when (rule 52).
Infinitive construct takes the verb giveth.
The suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes he (rule 18).
Partitive preposition takes of.
Noun takes seed.
Suffix takes his.
Preposition takes unto.
Assimilated article before Molech; the ASV writes no the (rules 12, 29).
Proper name.

The ASV recasts the purpose clause of levilti hamit as a coordinate one and states nothing of the preposition's own relation, so the lamed is unrepresented under rule 40; rule 14's closing sentence forbids making it the home for the supplied coordinator, and rule 52's inventory of what a lamed before an infinitive takes contains no coordinator.

The coordinating and is supplied for a clause in which no conjunction morpheme stands unrendered — the lamed is a preposition and bilti already holds its own not — so no morpheme licenses it (rule 14's count, rule 30). Rule 26's contrary treatment of an and reaches only the len X leY connective, which this is not.
The negative particle bilti takes not.
Infinitive takes put ... to death, discontinuous around the object pronoun and the negative (rule 25).
Object marker unrendered (rule 16).
Object suffix takes him.

review_notes: Corrected: the lamed of levilti hamit no longer holds the ASV's coordinating and. Rule 14's closing sentence is explicit that a preposition whose own relation the ASV leaves unstated is unrepresented under rule 40 rather than a home for a coordinator, and rule 26 confirms the default by carving out only the len X leY case. Counting the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's connectives leaves the and in surplus, so it is its own added unit.
The infinitive absolute takes at all and the finite verb keeps do ... hide (rule 56).
Only one determiner is written for ha-ish ha-hu; the demonstrative pronoun takes it and both articles are unrepresented.
